---
title: "How to read lfpack files"
---

## Pick a recording and a scale

A file can hold several recordings (e.g. every probe of a release) and several scales of each.

```python
from lfpack import LFPackReader

LFPackReader.recordings("multi.lf.h5")            # ['probe00', 'probe01']
LFPackReader.scales("multi.lf.h5", "probe00")     # [0]  (0 = full resolution)

sr = LFPackReader("multi.lf.h5", recording="probe00", scale=0)
```

`recording` can be omitted when the file holds a single one.

## Bin channels while reading

Neighbouring channels are strongly correlated at LFP frequencies. `bin_channels` sums groups
of adjacent channels during decoding, so a brain-wide sweep never materialises 384 channels:

```python
sr = LFPackReader("recording.lf.h5", bin_channels=4)
traces = sr[0:1000]                     # (1000, nc // 4)
sr.geometry["y"]                        # mean depth of each group
sr.geometry_full["binned_channel_index"]  # raw channel → group

sr.read_samples(0, 1000, bin_channels=8)  # per-call override
```

`bin_channels` must divide `nc`; `sr.channels` (brain locations) aggregates the same way.

## Session-clock times

Use `sr.times` rather than `np.arange(ns) / sr.fs` to align samples with trial events or
spikes: it applies the sync stored in the file.

## Format-1 files

Files written by lfpack < 1.0 (format 1) are still read transparently. Format 1 is
deprecated and will stop being readable in a future release; convert them with:

```python
import lfpack

lfpack.upgrade_h5("old.lf.h5", "new.lf.h5")   # no re-compression; 2.4× smaller at ε = 100, α = 14
```
